conventions.convention: The domain is an open subset of R^(n+1), n≥1. A one-form acts as a coordinate covector; nonsingularity means that covector is nonzero, and the horizontal space is its kernel.

Horizontal paths are continuous piecewise-C1 paths with finitely many pieces and ω(γ′)=0. Reversal, both time signs, constant paths and finite concatenations are allowed; reachability within V requires the entire path to remain in V.
An integrating factor is nowhere-zero μ∈C1(W) with μω=dS for S∈C2(W) and dS nowhere zero. It supplies neither global exactness nor physical entropy calibration.
The bracket is [X,Y]=DY·X−DX·Y; the flow variational equation is ∂tJ=DX(φX)J with J(0)=I.

The Frobenius equivalence compares existence of a neighborhood where ω∧dω vanishes with existence of a possibly smaller neighborhood carrying an exact nonzero multiple; vanishing merely at the base point is insufficient.
Closed means dω=0; globally exact means ω=dS for one globally defined C2 scalar. The period calculation uses γ(t)=(cos t,sin t), 0≤t≤2π, with counterclockwise orientation.

load_bearing.statement: Defines coordinate Ck one-forms, nonsingularity, Hq=ker ωq, differential and exterior products, coordinate exterior derivative, finite-piece horizontal paths, reachability within an open set, and local nowhere-zero integrating factors.

For X:U→R^m with continuous first partial derivatives on open U, m≥1, and q0∈U, there exist r,δ>0 and a flow on [−δ,δ]×closed B(q0,r/2), valued in closed B(q0,r), solving the IVP uniquely among solutions staying in that ball, with locally Lipschitz initial-point dependence and the local flow law whenever the displayed maps are defined in the chosen neighborhood.

For a C2 vector field X, its local flow is jointly C2 and its initial-point derivative satisfies the variational equation. For C2 fields X,Y, if [X,Y]=0 on a neighborhood and all local maps stay there, DφX^t(q)Y(q)=Y(φX^t(q)) and their local flows commute whenever both sides are defined.

For a C2 one-form on open U⊆R^(n+1), n≥1, nonzero at q0, the following local conditions at q0 are equivalent: ω∧dω=0 on some neighborhood; and dS=μω on some neighborhood for nowhere-zero μ∈C1 and S∈C2.

For a nowhere-zero C2 one-form on open U⊆R^(n+1), n≥1, assume every point has a neighborhood with dS=μω, S∈C2 and nowhere-zero μ∈C1. Every horizontal reachability class in U is contained in a countable union of compact subsets of U with empty interior. Every nonempty open V⊆U therefore contains a point not reachable from the chosen q even by a horizontal path in U. No global first integral or choice axiom is assumed.
Let U⊆R^(n+1) be open, ω a C1 one-form, μ∈C1(U) nowhere zero, and S∈C2(U) with dS=μω. Then ω∧dω=0 on U.
